## 1. HIGHLIGHTS

• Official visit of the South African President to Kinshasa to support the fight against the Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease outbreak and strengthen cooperation between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Africa.

• Forty-two (42) new confirmed cases including 7 community deaths were reported during the day of 02 July 2026, in the provinces of Ituri (33 cases including 5 deaths) and Nord-Kivu (9 cases cases including 2 deaths).
These confirmed cases come from the ZS (health zone) of Rwampara (14), Bunia (10), Mongbwalu (3), Bambu (2), Mandima (2), Lita (1), Tchomia (1), in Ituri and from Butembo (4), Katwa (2), Beni (2) and Kyondo (1) in Nord-Kivu.

• Fourteen (14) deaths were recorded among MVE (Ebola virus disease) patients in the CTE (Ebola treatment centre)/CT (transit centre) in the provinces of Ituri (6 at the CTE of Mongbwalu, 3 at the CTE of Bunia, 2 at the CTE of Rwampara, 1 at the CTE of ISTM and 1 at the CTE CME and of Nord-Kivu (1 at the CTE Katwa).

• Sixteen (16) patients with Ebola virus disease, including 15 in the province of Ituri (6 at the CTE Mongbwalu, 3 at the CTE CME, 3 at the CTE Bunia, 2 at the CT Bambu and 1 at the CTE Rwampara) and 1 at the CTE Katwa in the province of Nord-Kivu were declared cured after obtaining negative control tests.

• Installation of diagnostic laboratories in the health zones of Komanda, Nizi, Mambasa and Nia-Nia, in the province of Ituri.

## 2. EPIDEMIOLOGICAL AND OPERATIONAL CONTEXT

The province of Ituri, located in the north-east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, shares a long and porous border with Uganda and South Sudan.
For more than two decades, it has faced a chronic humanitarian crisis linked to armed conflicts and recurrent population displacements.
Its population is estimated at more than 8 million inhabitants, including more than one million internally displaced persons.
The Mongbwalu health zone, considered the starting point of the outbreak, is located in the Djugu territory 70 km from Bunia.
This zone is characterised by the presence of armed groups, frequent population movements towards Uganda, and numerous artisanal mining sites attracting migrant workers.
In September 2018, the province of Ituri had already been affected by the 10th MVE outbreak which was then raging in Nord-Kivu.
The current outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, was officially declared on 15 May 2026 by the Minister of Public Health.
The three affected provinces have a total population estimated at nearly 15 million inhabitants, with massive internal displacements and cross-border flows towards neighbouring countries.

3.3 Temporal analysis: An increasing number of confirmed cases is observed from one week to the next, reflecting continuous transmission of the disease in the community, although during epidemiological weeks 23 and 24, the number of cases appeared to be stable.
The intensification of public health actions in terms of epidemiological and biological surveillance (decentralisation of diagnostic capacities) contributed to early detection, confirming continuous and increased community transmission in W25.
Compared to all weeks where cases have been recorded since the beginning of the outbreak, W25 and W26 represent the peak so far, amounting to more than 300 weekly cases.

During the last 24 hours, 42 new confirmed cases and 21 deaths were recorded in the provinces of Ituri (33 cases and 18 deaths) and Nord-Kivu (9 cases and 3 deaths), highlighting the progression of the epidemiological situation of the 17th Ebola Virus Disease (MVE) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Thus, the cumulative total rises to 1 502 confirmed cases and 473 deaths, expressing an overall case fatality rate of 31,6%.

Provincial dynamics and concentration of cases

The province of Ituri alone concentrates 90,9% of cases (n=1 366) and 83,9% of deaths (n=398), representing a case fatality rate of 29,1%, making it the absolute epicentre of the outbreak.
The health zones of Bunia (426 cases), Rwampara (322 cases) and Mongbwalu (273 cases) remain the most affected and concentrate approximately 67,9% of cases reported at the provincial level and 74,7% at the national level.
In these same ZS, moderate case fatality rates were observed in the ZS of Rwampara (20,8%) and Bunia (25,1%), whilst the zone of Mongbwalu also combines a high case fatality rate, amounting to 49,8% (136 deaths for 273 cases), suggesting persistent challenges in early case management or access to care.
It should be noted that 17 additional cases (without associated death) were reported whilst the health zones of origin remain to be identified, which could indicate a geographical expansion requiring strengthened investigation.

Severity of the outbreak in Nord-Kivu

A total of 133 confirmed cases and 75 deaths has been reported in the province of Nord-Kivu since the beginning of the outbreak, representing a case fatality rate of 56,4 %.
The latter presents the most concerning profile in terms of severity, with a case fatality rate well above the national average.
This high case fatality rate is driven by the health zones of Katwa (68,6%), Oicha (66,7%), Kyondo (66,7%) and Beni (57,1%).
The health zone of Katwa comes first in notifications in terms of number of cases (n=53), followed by the ZS of Butembo (n=38) with a case fatality rate of 42,1%.
A case fatality rate of 100% was observed exceptionally in the health zone of Vuhovi (with low numbers).

### 4.9. Security

• The security situation remains calm but unpredictable in Bunia and surroundings.

• The incident that occurred at PK51 in the ZS of Nia-Nia slowed down scheduled activities.
Strengthening dialogue with local authorities, community leaders and security services remains a priority to guarantee access to high-risk areas.

### 4.10. PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse)

Ituri : Sensitization activities and installation of PSEA materials reached 231 persons, including 180 women and 51 men at the Governorate, in markets, at the Tséré site and in several health
facilities in Bunia and Rwampara.
Actions included distribution of advice cards, posting of messages and community sensitization.

## 5. MAIN CHALLENGES, IMPACTS AND REQUIRED ACTIONS


| No. | Challenges | Impact | Actions required |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reluctance towards post-mortem sampling (EDS / swabs) and community resistance | Delayed confirmation, underestimation of cases, disruption of key activities | Intensify CREC, involvement of religious and community leaders, strengthening of team safety |
| 2 | Insufficient CTE capacity and saturation in Nord-Kivu (138,8%) | Admission delays, increased risk of nosocomial transmission | Accelerate construction and expansion of CTEs, deploy additional temporary structures |
| 3 | Suboptimal contact follow-up performance (81,3% vs target 95%) | Transmission chains not interrupted | Train, deploy and motivate community health workers (RECO), strengthened supervision |
| 4 | Low escalation of alerts in certain affected ZS | Undetected transmission, silent expansion of the outbreak | Strengthen community surveillance, improve rapid escalation and investigation of alerts |
| 5 | Confirmed cases not yet broken down by health zone (17 cases) | Major gaps in the reconstruction of transmission chains | Conduct data reconciliation, weed out possible duplicates, and reclassify or specify health zone and status (deaths, cured, active, etc.) Active field verification |
| 6 | Insufficient supply of MEG and medical inputs | Weakening of overall care | Advocacy and urgent supply of essential medicines |
| 7 | Insufficient PCI inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited training | High risk of nosocomial infections (96 HCW cases including 19 deaths, case fatality rate 19,7%) | Urgent supply, strengthening of PCI training |
| 8 | Stock of samples not yet analysed (backlog) in the laboratory in Nord-Kivu and late diagnosis | Delayed confirmation, high case fatality rate (54,2%) | Deploy a laboratory catch-up plan, strengthen diagnostic capacities |
| 9 | Insufficient ambulances and isolation structures (gap of 20 centres) | Transfer and isolation delays, increased risk of transmission | Urgent deployment of logistical resources and additional infrastructure |
| 10 | Insufficient coordination and low use of COUSP frameworks | Operational inefficiency and delayed decisions | Strengthen coordination mechanisms at all levels, operationalise provincial COUSPs |
| 11 | Insufficient financial resources (gap of 20 million USD) | Limitation of implementation of all response pillars | Urgent resource mobilisation, advocacy with partners |
| 12 | Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) | Restriction of operations, limited access to high-risk areas | Strengthening of security coordination and humanitarian access |
| 13 | Continuity of essential services (CEHS) compromised | Increase in indirect mortality (non-Ebola) | Effective implementation of free healthcare, strengthening of CEHS |
| 14 | High population mobility | High risk of rapid geographical expansion | Strengthen surveillance at PoE/PoC and cross-border coordination |
